sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, episode 139, Scientific Python, with Guido Imperial.
sentences.zh: Programming Throwdown，第139期，科学计算 Python，嘉宾是 Guido Imperial。

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: 交给你了，Jason。

sentences.en: Hey, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: So if you're following Hacker News or you're following these various sources, you've probably heard about Scientific Python.
sentences.zh: 如果你有关注 Hacker News 或者其他各类信息源，你可能已经听说过“科学计算 Python”（Scientific Python）。

sentences.en: It's becoming a really important way for people to try and do numerical computation and solve really difficult probleMs.
sentences.zh: 它正成为人们进行数值计算和解决极高难度问题的一种非常重要的方式。

sentences.en: There's a bunch of really awesome libraries for that.
sentences.zh: 为此，社区里涌现了一大批非常棒的库。

sentences.en: We'll definitely cover that in detail.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会详细介绍这些内容。

sentences.en: And we have Guido Imperiale here from Coiled to tell us kind of more about it.
sentences.zh: 今天我们请到了来自 Coiled 的 Guido Imperiale，让他为我们深入讲解一下。

sentences.en: So Guido is an open source software engineer for Coiled.
sentences.zh: Guido 是 Coiled 的一名开源软件工程师。

sentences.en: And I think we're all really grateful for having Guido on the show to lend us his experience and expertise.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都很感谢 Guido 能来到节目，分享他的经验和专业知识。

sentences.en: So thanks for coming on the show, Guido.
sentences.zh: 感谢你参加我们的节目，Guido。

sentences.en: Hi, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So before we dive into what is Scientific Python, why don't you give us some background about what have you been up to?
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨什么是科学计算 Python 之前，能不能先介绍一下你的背景，以及你最近在忙些什么？

sentences.en: What kind of led you to Coiled?
sentences.zh: 是什么契机让你加入了 Coiled？

sentences.en: And how did you get involved in, you know, in Dask and in the overall SciPy community?
sentences.zh: 你是如何接触到 Dask 以及整个 SciPy 社区的？

sentences.en: Well, I have done something years in risk management, in banking and insurances in Italy and UK.
sentences.zh: 我在意大利和英国的银行及保险业从事风险管理工作多年。

sentences.en: And what risk management is about is simulate financial instruments or the whole balance sheet many, many times.
sentences.zh: 风险管理的核心工作就是对金融工具或整个资产负债表进行多次模拟。

sentences.en: And a lot of financial institutions use obscure closed source software, which tends to be very, very slow and inefficient and really unwieldy.
sentences.zh: 许多金融机构都在使用晦涩难懂的闭源软件，这些软件往往运行非常缓慢、效率低下，而且极其笨重。

sentences.en: So in one of my previous jobs, I was faced with this software and I decided, nope, I'm going to rewrite it from zero.
sentences.zh: 在之前的一份工作中，我遇到了这种软件，于是我决定：不行，我要从零开始重写它。

sentences.en: And I needed a really, really big hammer to break down the problem.
sentences.zh: 我需要一把非常强力的“大锤”来攻克这个难题。

sentences.en: And I realized that Dask was just right.
sentences.zh: 后来我意识到，Dask 正是最佳选择。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: So why don't you dive into that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 能不能详细讲讲这个过程？

sentences.en: So I've heard stories of banks running their own version of Python.
sentences.zh: 我听说过一些银行运行自己定制版 Python 的故事。

sentences.en: I think, Patrick, you mentioned this in an earlier episode.
sentences.zh: Patrick，我想你在之前的节目里提到过这个。

sentences.en: There's like Bank Python or something like that.
sentences.zh: 好像叫什么“银行版 Python”（Bank Python）之类的。

sentences.en: And so what about closed source software at the companies you were at?
sentences.zh: 那么你所在公司使用的那些闭源软件是怎么回事？

sentences.en: What about it was sort of unwieldy and difficult to use?
sentences.zh: 它们在哪些方面显得笨重且难以使用？

sentences.en: First of all, it was a piece of software designed 30 years ago, back when multi-threading was not a thing.
sentences.zh: 首先，那是一款 30 年前设计的软件，那时候多线程技术还没出现。

sentences.en: So first of all, it's all traditional design of have an iteration on a single point, go through to the whole depth and then go back.
sentences.zh: 所以它采用的是传统的单点迭代设计，必须遍历整个深度，然后再返回。

sentences.en: It had no benefit whatsoever from a SIMD and AVX or parallel multi-threading.
sentences.zh: 它完全无法利用 SIMD、AVX 指令集或并行多线程带来的任何优势。

sentences.en: It would be really, really painful.
sentences.zh: 那过程真的非常非常痛苦。

sentences.en: It was written in C++, but that was the only saving grace.
sentences.zh: 它虽然是用 C++ 编写的，但这已经是它唯一的优点了。

sentences.en: And then that was the simulation part of the software.
sentences.zh: 那是软件的模拟部分。

sentences.en: The aggregation part was written in Java and it was even worse.
sentences.zh: 而聚合部分是用 Java 写的，情况甚至更糟。

sentences.en: To give an order of magnitude, the reporting part was taking five days over to run every
sentences.zh: 举个量级参考，报告生成部分每次运行需要五天时间，

sentences.en: time, five days exercise with two people who did nothing else but throw kicks at the software whenever it was hanging.
sentences.zh: 这五天里，有两个人什么都不做，专门盯着软件，一旦卡死就得去重启它。

sentences.en: And it was running on 20 hosts with 380 gigabytes of RAM each.
sentences.zh: 而且它是在 20 台主机上运行的，每台主机都有 380GB 的内存。

sentences.en: We are talking about now 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们现在谈论的是 10 年前的情况。

sentences.en: So that was expensive hardware.
sentences.zh: 那可是相当昂贵的硬件。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's wild.
sentences.zh: 确实，太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And I came, I saw, I rewrote.
sentences.zh: 我来了，我见了，我重写了。

sentences.en: And by the time I left five years later, that exact same algorithm instead of five days and the 380 gigabytes of RAM was running in two hours and 20 gig.
sentences.zh: 当我五年后离开时，同样的算法，不再需要五天和 380GB 内存，只需要两个小时和 20GB 内存就能跑完。

sentences.en: So, so this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: So you saw this, you know, huge Java C++, you know, kind of monolith, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你面对的是一个庞大的 Java 和 C++ 单体架构，对吧？

sentences.en: And yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, it's really inefficient.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它真的非常低效。

sentences.en: How do you get started on a project like that?
sentences.zh: 你是如何着手处理这样一个项目的？

sentences.en: I mean, do you sit down and write a document explaining every bit and piece?
sentences.zh: 你是坐下来写一份文档解释每一个细节吗？

sentences.en: Do you start by converting small pieces?
sentences.zh: 还是从转换小模块开始？

sentences.en: Like, how do you go about doing such a transformation?
sentences.zh: 你是如何进行这种转型的？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: First of all, in any such kind of environment where you have a massive piece of software,
sentences.zh: 首先，在任何拥有庞大软件的环境中，

sentences.en: that legacy software that you need to tackle, forget about rewriting the whole thing in one go.
sentences.zh: 面对那些需要处理的遗留软件，千万别想着一口气全部重写。

sentences.en: You just can't.
sentences.zh: 你根本做不到。

sentences.en: You will fail.
sentences.zh: 你会失败的。

sentences.en: You will end up in a five years long project that never delivers and management will put the plug on it.
sentences.zh: 你最终会陷入一个长达五年的项目，永远无法交付，管理层也会直接砍掉它。

sentences.en: Guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 这是肯定的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it is imperative to follow a bit of mantra of agile and deliver as small a piece as you can every time to keep stakeholders happy.
sentences.zh: 所以，遵循敏捷开发的原则至关重要，每次只交付尽可能小的模块，以保持利益相关者的满意度。

sentences.en: And that piece needs to integrate as good as possible with the legacy software.
sentences.zh: 而且这些模块需要尽可能好地与遗留软件集成。

sentences.en: And yes, that means that you will have a 20% of throwaway code, but it's the way to go
sentences.zh: 是的，这意味着你会有 20% 的代码是最终会被丢弃的，但这是必经之路，

sentences.en: because at all times during this transformation process, which takes in the end, it takes five years.
sentences.zh: 因为在整个转型过程中（最终耗时五年），

sentences.en: Don't get me wrong.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思。

sentences.en: Stakeholders can see, oh, now this little piece was rubbish and now it's super fast and super stable and they start getting their appetite wet for the next big thing.
sentences.zh: 利益相关者能看到：哦，原来这一小块代码是垃圾，现在变得超快、超稳定了，他们就会开始对下一个大目标充满期待。

sentences.en: And they will be happy to keep bankrolling your project.
sentences.zh: 他们会很乐意继续为你的项目提供资金。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 确实有道理。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think one of the challenges is where you have, there's this sort of meme.
sentences.zh: 我觉得其中一个挑战是，业界存在一种梗。

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, there's 18 different messaging platforMs.
sentences.zh: 就像是：现在有 18 种不同的消息平台，

sentences.en: I want to make one that unifies them all.
sentences.zh: 我想做一个统一所有平台的平台。

sentences.en: Now there's 19 platforMs.
sentences.zh: 结果现在有了 19 种平台。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so you're going to, in the short term, kind of add another piece.
sentences.zh: 所以短期内，你实际上是增加了一个新的组件。

sentences.en: Actually, so this new, the rewrite that you did was that, that was using Dask and Python, correct?
sentences.zh: 那么，你所做的重写工作是使用了 Dask 和 Python，对吧？

sentences.en: And DexArray, yes.
sentences.zh: 还有 Dask Array，是的。

sentences.en: Okay, got it.
sentences.zh: 好的，明白了。

sentences.en: So there was a moment there where you had to kind of convince people to add another language and add, you know, complexity to that project.
sentences.zh: 所以当时你肯定经历过一个阶段，需要说服人们引入另一种语言，增加项目的复杂性。

sentences.en: How did you go about doing that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: That was actually easy because I did not start from Dask.
sentences.zh: 其实那部分很容易，因为我并不是从 Dask 开始的。

sentences.en: That project was around this third-party software within C++ and Java.
sentences.zh: 那个项目围绕着 C++ 和 Java 的第三方软件展开。

sentences.en: There was an ungodly amount of Bash and Perl scripting and which if anybody had the pleasure to work with it in a serious amount, serious size, it's impossible to deal with.
sentences.zh: 里面有海量的 Bash 和 Perl 脚本，如果有人试过在一定规模下使用它们，就会发现根本无法处理。

sentences.en: As soon as you get beyond two pages of code, Bash becomes unusable.
sentences.zh: 一旦代码超过两页，Bash 就变得不可用了。

sentences.en: It becomes untestable and really, really hard to read.
sentences.zh: 它变得无法测试，而且非常非常难读。

sentences.en: If you have a newbie programmer on the team, they will not understand why with parentheses space works and parentheses without space doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 如果团队里有个新手程序员，他们根本搞不懂为什么带括号加空格能运行，而不带空格就不行。

sentences.en: So it's really, really bad.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: And Perl is, well, I mean, there are actual competition about obfuscating Perl and I leave it at that.
sentences.zh: 至于 Perl，怎么说呢，甚至还有专门关于混淆 Perl 代码的比赛，我就不多说了。

sentences.en: But I've seen Perl soft, I've seen things that you mortals cannot even comprehend.
sentences.zh: 但我见过 Perl 软件，我见过凡人无法理解的东西。

sentences.en: I've seen Perl programs that generate at runtime Perl regular expressions worth five pages, which are then fed into a second Perl interpreter to parse the actual content.
sentences.zh: 我见过在运行时生成五页长 Perl 正则表达式的程序，然后把这些代码喂给第二个 Perl 解释器来解析实际内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is brutal.

sentences.en: It's insane.
sentences.zh: 简直疯了。

sentences.en: It's insane.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So that was the situation I came in and I realized, nope.
sentences.zh: 这就是我接手时的状况，我意识到：不行。

sentences.en: And I started rewriting piece by piece, script by script.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始逐个脚本、逐个模块地进行重写。

sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是成千上万个独立的小脚本，全部用 Python 重写，并在上面添加工具，或者针对客户的特定工具。

sentences.en: Some of which by now, by the way, it is now open source.

sentences.en: So, it was very easy to take one out and put the replacement in which was like for like just better working, faster, easier to maintain with unit tests and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 所以，把旧的拿出来，换上新的，实现相同的功能但运行更好、更快、更易维护，还带有单元测试等等，这非常容易。

sentences.en: And by the time I replaced the majority of those, I had a common library that was in the common
sentences.zh: 当我替换掉大部分脚本时，我就拥有了一个公共库，

sentences.zh: 公共工具，以及整个团队（10 个人）对 Python 语言的共同学习成果，我说：好的，现在我们有了坚实的基础。

sentences.en: Python language, which I say, okay, now we have a solid foundation.

sentences.zh: Pandas 专门用于表格数据的操作。

sentences.en: There's Pandas, there's NumPy that is below Pandas, but is also, uh, has a different scope.
sentences.zh: 所以你以前用 Excel，现在用 Pandas，它在各个方面都更好，但看起来和用起来仍然像 Excel。

sentences.en: So Pandas is all about data manipulation for tabular data manipulation specifically.
sentences.zh: 而 NumPy 则是关于矩阵计算和这种重度向量化算法，这些算法可能具有许多可以沿其移动的维度。

sentences.en: So you, you, you were using Excel and now you're using Pandas and it's better in every possible way, but it still looks and feel like Excel.
sentences.zh: 而且两者之间有很高的互操作性。

sentences.en: NumPy instead is about matricial computations and this kind of heavily vectorized algorithms that have potentially many, many dimensions that you can move along.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，Pandas 是建立在 NumPy 之上的。

sentences.en: And there is very high interoperability between the two.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以拥有一个运行在 Pandas 上的高级 NumPy 算法。

sentences.en: Again, Pandas is built on top of NumPy.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you can have an advanced NumPy algorithm that runs on Pandas.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: SciPy is also on top of NumPy.
sentences.zh: SciPy 也是建立在 NumPy 之上的。

sentences.en: It's just extra functions that are more niche, like statistical, statistical analysis and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 它只是一些更细分、更专业的额外函数，比如统计学、统计分析之类的。

sentences.en: If you put everything together, you will end up with something that somewhat resembles R,
sentences.zh: 如果你把所有东西整合在一起，最终得到的东西会有点像 R 语言，

sentences.en: although R is still king when it comes with, with really, really exotic algorithm that only exists in one paper circa 1996.
sentences.zh: 尽管在处理那些 1996 年左右仅存在于某篇论文中的、非常非常冷门的算法时，R 依然是王者。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That paper had a code attached to it and you can guarantee that code is in R.
sentences.zh: 那篇论文附带了代码，而且你可以肯定那代码是用 R 写的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a good way of explaining it.
sentences.zh: 这个解释很到位。

sentences.en: So yeah, at a high level, you know, the, the reason people use Excel is because tables are probably the easiest way to think in a vector with a vector mindset, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，从宏观层面来看，人们使用 Excel 的原因在于，表格可能是以向量思维来思考问题的最简单方式，对吧？

sentences.en: And the reason why that's important is because if you do an operation on a vector, you know,
sentences.zh: 之所以这很重要，是因为如果你对一个向量进行操作，你知道，

sentences.en: that vector can be very large or even unbounded, uh, you could work with it in an atomic way.
sentences.zh: 那个向量可能非常大，甚至是无限的，你可以以原子化的方式处理它。

sentences.en: So for example, you know, if you look at R or MATLAB, you can have two matrices.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你看看 R 或 MATLAB，你可以有两个矩阵。

sentences.en: The matrices can be high, really high dimensional, even arbitrary number of dimensions with respect to your, your program, and you can just do A plus B.
sentences.zh: 这些矩阵可以是高维的，维度非常高，甚至对于你的程序来说是任意维度的，你只需要执行 A 加 B 即可。

sentences.en: And as long as the dimensions are equivalent, um, or even sometimes if they're not, there'll be some fan out operation, but, but in general,
sentences.zh: 只要维度相同，或者有时即使维度不同，也会进行某种广播操作，但总的来说，

sentences.en: you know, as long as the A and B have the same dimensions, you just do A literally in your code, you write A plus B and you get the sum of those two.
sentences.zh: 只要 A 和 B 的维度相同，你只需在代码里写 A 加 B，就能得到两者的和。

sentences.en: The other part of it is, and people can try this.
sentences.zh: 另一部分是，大家可以试一试。

sentences.en: If you grab Octave, which is the open source MATLAB, or if you grab MATLAB and you do, you have two vectors, you do A plus B, they'll be done like super, super fast, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你用 Octave（开源版的 MATLAB），或者用 MATLAB，你有两个向量，执行 A 加 B，它们会算得超级超级快，对吧？

sentences.en: You can also write a for loop in MATLAB and you can say, you know, for I zero to the size of the vector, you know, C is equal to,
sentences.zh: 你也可以在 MATLAB 里写一个 for 循环，比如，从 0 到向量大小的循环，C 等于，

sentences.en: C of I is equal to A of I plus B of I.
sentences.zh: C 的第 i 个元素等于 A 的第 i 个元素加上 B 的第 i 个元素。

sentences.en: And that will take forever, right?
sentences.zh: 那会慢到天荒地老，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, so what the reason is because when you do A plus B under the hood, it's not just a for loop, it's doing a million other
sentences.zh: 所以原因在于，当你执行 A 加 B 时，底层不仅仅是一个 for 循环，它还在做一百万件其他事情，

sentences.en: things to make that addition super, super faSt. Like it's taking advantage of the different process,
sentences.zh: 来让加法变得超级超级快。比如它利用了不同的处理器，

sentences.en: like a coprocessors and your processor, like the SIMD and these other coprocessors, it might be running on the GPU, you know, depending on if you're using something like JAX or
sentences.zh: 比如协处理器和你的主处理器，像 SIMD 和其他协处理器，它甚至可能在 GPU 上运行，你知道，取决于你是否在使用 JAX 之类的工具，

sentences.en: one of these things, it'll actually farm that out to the GPU, the graphics processing unit.
sentences.zh: 或者类似的东西，它实际上会把任务分发到 GPU，即图形处理器上。

sentences.en: Or even in the case of Dask, it might send that part of that sum to another machine or to many other machines, and then go and collect the output.
sentences.zh: 甚至在 Dask 的情况下，它可能会把求和任务的一部分发送到另一台机器或多台机器上，然后再去收集输出结果。

sentences.en: And so in all of these cases, you know, you're able to work at a really high level.
sentences.zh: 所以在所有这些情况下，你都能在很高的层面上工作。

sentences.en: And you're able to do the same operation many, many times on many different data atoms very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 并且能够非常非常快地对大量不同的数据原子重复执行相同的操作。

sentences.en: And that's something that Excel also gives you, you know, in Excel, you can say sum A.
sentences.zh: 这也是 Excel 能带给你的，在 Excel 里，你可以说求和 A 列。

sentences.en: It's very, very terse, it's very fast, and it sums the entire column super quickly.
sentences.zh: 它非常简洁，速度非常快，能瞬间算出整列的和。

sentences.en: So it's all kind of with that kind of a mindset that we can get a lot of stuff done without having to be experts on the GPU and SIMD and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正是带着这种思维，无需成为 GPU、SIMD 等方面的专家，就能完成很多工作。

sentences.en: Yes, except that there are two big things to point out.
sentences.zh: 没错，但有两点大问题需要指出。

sentences.en: The first one is that the amount of library that is available for Excel is a tiny fraction of what you have on NumPy.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，Excel 可用的库数量只是 NumPy 的一小部分。

sentences.en: And the second big thing is reproducibility.
sentences.zh: 第二个大问题是可重复性。

sentences.en: So one of the biggest problems with Excel is that you have your VBA code and your in-cell formulas mixed with your data.
sentences.zh: Excel 最大的问题之一就是你的 VBA 代码和单元格公式与数据混在一起。

sentences.en: And as soon as your data changes, you will need to start thinking, okay, how do I keep my software meaning my VBA and my in-cell formulas while swapping the data?
sentences.zh: 一旦数据发生变化，你就得开始思考：我该如何在替换数据的同时保留我的软件（即 VBA 和单元格公式）？

sentences.en: And for a regular piece of software that's trivial, the software is the software, the data is the data.
sentences.zh: 对于常规软件来说，这很简单，软件就是软件，数据就是数据。

sentences.en: And you have a command that says software.py or .exe, input file, output file, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一条命令，比如 software.py 或 .exe，输入文件，输出文件，诸如此类。

sentences.en: In Excel, it's not like that.
sentences.zh: 但在 Excel 里，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: It's the same file.
sentences.zh: 它们是同一个文件。

sentences.en: And I've seen the most horrible things to work around that.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，我见过最可怕的操作。

sentences.en: And inevitably,
sentences.zh: 而且不可避免地，

sentences.en: you will end up with human error with stuff that simply stops working because the software has been corrupted by new data or something bad like that.
sentences.zh: 你会因为人为错误而导致程序停止工作，因为软件被新数据破坏了，或者发生了类似糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Or there was a manual step in updating the data that was not performed just right.
sentences.zh: 又或者在更新数据时有一个手动步骤没做对。

sentences.en: And now there is a subtle difference in the output that you will not notice because you forgot a validation step that will be otherwise redundant.
sentences.zh: 现在输出结果出现了一个细微的差异，而你却没注意到，因为你漏掉了一个本该多余的验证步骤。

sentences.en: So that's a colossal problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And then you have, how do you put Excel code in version control?
sentences.zh: 还有，你怎么把 Excel 代码放入版本控制？

sentences.en: The short answer is you just commit a binary blob.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：你只能提交一个二进制大对象（blob）。

sentences.en: Now there is a change.
sentences.zh: 现在有了一个改动。

sentences.en: Put a new binary blob into version control.
sentences.zh: 把新的二进制大对象放入版本控制。

sentences.en: What changed?
sentences.zh: 改了什么？

sentences.en: Well, you have two binary blobs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你有两个二进制大对象。

sentences.en: Can't you tell the difference?
sentences.zh: 你看不出区别吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And again, I've seen the most exotic solutions where there were macros that were yanking all the VBA code out of an Excel spreadsheet, saving them to version control,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我见过最离谱的解决方案，有人写了宏把所有 VBA 代码从 Excel 表格里提取出来，保存到版本控制中，

sentences.en: and then another macro that was yanking them back in and rebuilding the spreadsheet was nightmare.
sentences.zh: 然后再用另一个宏把它们导回去重建表格，简直是噩梦。

sentences.en: Speaking of nightmare, do you want a horror story?
sentences.zh: 说到噩梦，你想听个恐怖故事吗？

sentences.en: Sure, let's hear it.
sentences.zh: 当然，说来听听。

sentences.en: I actually was thinking of, I have a horror story in my head, but I'd love to hear yours firSt. It's probably more horrific, and then people can ramp down at my story.
sentences.zh: 我其实正想着，我脑子里有个恐怖故事，但我很想先听听你的。你的可能更恐怖，然后大家听完我的故事就能缓一缓了。

sentences.zh: 那是，我记得，四页的 VBA 代码。

sentences.zh: 两小时后，他回来，祈祷着它能给出结果。

sentences.zh: 40 毫秒后，程序运行结束。

sentences.zh: 他看着我。

sentences.zh: 我说，噢，我不知道你还能这么做。

sentences.zh: 我也有个类似的故事，

sentences.zh: 我要把我妹夫拿出来当反面教材。

sentences.zh: 我妹夫数学非常非常好。

sentences.en: And, and, and I remember this is years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且，我记得那是很多年前的事了。

sentences.zh: 那时我们俩都还是相对初级的职场新人。

sentences.en: And, um, he asked me to take a look at his laptop because of course, everyone with a CS degree is also an expert in it, right?
sentences.zh: 他让我帮他看看笔记本电脑，因为当然了，每个有计算机科学学位的人也都是 IT 专家，对吧？

sentences.en: In your family.
sentences.zh: 在你的家庭里。

sentences.en: So I was really prepared to not have any solution for this because I'm usually terrible at it, but, but it was just,
sentences.zh: 所以我当时已经准备好解决不了这个问题了，因为我通常在这方面很烂，但，但其实就是，

sentences.en: he said it was running really slowly and he had, I'm not even kidding.
sentences.zh: 他说电脑运行得很慢，我没开玩笑，

sentences.en: It must've been over 200 Excel programs open at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他当时同时打开了超过 200 个 Excel 程序。

sentences.en: And almost all of the files had almost exactly the same name.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎所有文件的名字都一模一样。

sentences.en: And basically he had created, as you said, you know, he had this, this code that did all of this logic, but he wanted to run it, you know, on a hundred different data sets.
sentences.zh: 基本上他创建了，正如你所说，他写了这段代码来处理所有逻辑，但他想在一百个不同的数据集上运行它。

sentences.en: And so, you know, as a, as an economist, he didn't know how to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一个经济学家，他不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: So he created, you know, a hundred copies of this Excel spreadsheet.
sentences.zh: 于是他创建了一百个 Excel 表格的副本。

sentences.en: And then he just had them all, it was more than a hundred had them all open at the same time.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们全部，其实不止一百个，全部同时打开。

sentences.en: And he was trying to copy and paste data into each one.
sentences.zh: 他正试图把数据复制粘贴到每一个文件里。

sentences.en: And, uh, uh, I was like, you have to learn R I was like, I was like, I, at the time, I don't know how popular pandas was.
sentences.zh: 我当时就说，你得学 R。我当时，我不知道那时候 Pandas 有多流行。

sentences.en: Um, I don't even know how old pandas is.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道 Pandas 有多老了。

sentences.en: So I didn't know about any of that, but I've had told him, I said, you know, you have to learn R and get a book on R.
sentences.zh: 所以我对那些一无所知，但我告诉他，我说，你得学 R，去买本 R 的书。

sentences.en: Uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, to your point, your people get in sort of trapped in, in Excel and then it becomes, uh, difficult for them to take the next step.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说到点子上了，人们被困在 Excel 里，然后他们就很难迈出下一步。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of where I think scientific, uh, Python, that's, that's where I think it can grow the most is, uh, is, is with that audience, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为科学 Python 的增长潜力就在这里，就在这群受众身上，对吧？

sentences.en: The Excel audience.
sentences.zh: Excel 的用户群体。

sentences.en: So how do people, let's say, you know, people out there like, like my brother-in-law and like other people who might be really good with, with Excel,
sentences.zh: 那么，人们，比如说，像我妹夫那样的人，还有其他可能非常擅长 Excel 的人，

sentences.en: how do they get started with, with scientific Python?
sentences.zh: 他们该如何开始学习科学 Python 呢？

sentences.en: Like what's a way they can ramp into that?
sentences.zh: 有什么方法可以让他们入门吗？

sentences.en: There are plenty of tutorials out there.
sentences.zh: 市面上有很多教程。

sentences.en: First they would, they should start with the Python tutorial, which is generic and it teaches them like basic for loops.
sentences.zh: 首先他们应该从 Python 基础教程开始，那是通用的，会教他们基本的 for 循环。

sentences.en: And already that will give them the tools to awkwardly read a CSV file, do some calculations on it, and then write it out.
sentences.zh: 光是这些就足以让他们笨拙地读取 CSV 文件，做些计算，然后写出结果。

sentences.en: And then from there, they should start with a Pandas tutorial specific for scientific Python and realize that all that
sentences.zh: 然后从那里开始，他们应该学习专门针对科学 Python 的 Pandas 教程，并意识到他们之前用纯 Python 写的那个

sentences.en: for loop that they've wrote in pure Python, where they were opening the CSV file and reading cell by cell and calculating cell by cell, actually that becomes three lines in Pandas.
sentences.zh: for 循环，那种打开 CSV 文件、逐个单元格读取并逐个计算的方式，在 Pandas 里其实只需要三行代码。

sentences.en: And it's a lot faster as well.
sentences.zh: 而且速度快得多。

sentences.en: One thing that's different, you know, with Excel, it's, it's reactive, right?
sentences.zh: 有一点不同，你知道，Excel 是响应式的，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, with Pandas, it's imperative, right?
sentences.zh: 而 Pandas 是命令式的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, with Excel, you change the data and then the answer just magically appears, right?
sentences.zh: 在 Excel 里，你修改数据，答案就会神奇地自动出现，对吧？

sentences.en: And so how do you get people to sort of make that paradigm shift from, you know, everything is reactive and, and, and sort of, uh, it's like a, Excel is like a true functional
sentences.zh: 那么你如何让人们完成这种范式转换呢？从一切都是响应式的，Excel 就像一种真正的函数式编程语言，

sentences.en: programming language, right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: How do you go from that to something like Pandas where it's, you know, a script where you read it in the data, you know, how do you get people to make that paradigm shift?
sentences.zh: 你如何从那种模式转向像 Pandas 这样的东西，即一个读取数据的脚本？你如何让人们完成这种范式转换？

sentences.en: I think that for anybody that uses Excel professionally, reproducibility and removing human error is the cell.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于任何专业使用 Excel 的人来说，可重复性和消除人为错误就是卖点。

sentences.en: Yes, Excel is reactive, which is great if you want to prototype something, but then if you want to repeat the same operation every other week, and you want to repeat it exactly
sentences.zh: 没错，Excel 是响应式的，如果你想做原型设计，这很棒，但如果你想每隔一周重复相同的操作，并且想以完全相同的方式重复它，

sentences.en: the same way, and you want your replacement to repeat it the day that you're on holiday,
sentences.zh: 并且想让你休假时的替补人员也能重复同样的操作，

sentences.en: Excel is doom, is, you will get it wrong.
sentences.zh: Excel 就是灾难，你一定会出错。

sentences.zh: 除非你有某种高级配置，否则求和通常会使用单个CPU。

sentences.en: Well, as soon as you start finishing loading the first one, do the partial sum of that column that you want.

sentences.en: And how long have you been there?
sentences.zh: 你已经在那里待了多久了？

sentences.en: Coiled has been around for, I believe, a year and a half.
sentences.zh: Coiled 成立大概有一年半了。

sentences.en: And I've been there for a year.
sentences.zh: 我已经在那里待了一年了。

sentences.en: Actually, a year, a year and a half now.
sentences.zh: 其实，一年，现在是一年半了。

sentences.en: Two years the company, a year and a half me.
sentences.zh: 公司两年，我一年半。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So about how many people are there now?
sentences.zh: 那现在大概有多少人？

sentences.en: Uh, around 50 something.
sentences.zh: 呃，大概 50 多人吧。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And is it, I know it's, it's remote.
sentences.zh: 我知道它是远程办公的。

sentences.en: Is it, is it concentrated in the EU?
sentences.zh: 它是集中在欧盟吗？

sentences.en: Is it really all over?
sentences.zh: 还是遍布全球？

sentences.en: It's most of the people just happen to be in the US, but now we have a half dozen people in the EU, one in India.
sentences.zh: 大多数人恰好在美国，但现在我们在欧盟有六个人，印度有一个。

sentences.en: We used to have a couple in Australia that turned out to be problematic because our company meetings were at 6am in the morning for them, which was not really sustainable.
sentences.zh: 我们过去在澳大利亚有几位员工，但后来发现这行不通，因为对他们来说，我们的公司会议是在凌晨6点，这实在难以持续。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这很有道理。

sentences.en: So it's been around for a couple of years, about 50 people.
sentences.zh: 所以公司成立大概几年了，有50人左右。

sentences.en: I mean, that's actually a lot of growth.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这其实增长很快。

sentences.en: I mean, to go from zero to 50 in two years, it takes a lot of coordination to get that many people onboarded.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，两年内从零增长到50人，要让这么多人入职需要大量的协调工作。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a person every two weeks.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，平均每两周就有一名新员工。

sentences.en: Yeah, very cool.
sentences.zh: 没错，太棒了。

sentences.en: So are you, um, what's, what's sort of the plans going forward?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们未来的计划是什么样的？

sentences.en: Are you hiring full-time?
sentences.zh: 你们在招聘全职员工吗？

sentences.en: Are you hiring, uh, interns, all of the above, none of the above?
sentences.zh: 你们在招聘实习生吗，还是以上都有，或者以上都不是？

sentences.en: I don't believe we are hiring interns right now.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们现在在招实习生。

sentences.en: We have a page with careers.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个招聘页面。

sentences.en: If you want to have a look at it, if you want to send your CV, you are more than welcome.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看看，或者想投递简历，我们非常欢迎。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: And so what, what time zones are you supporting?
sentences.zh: 那么你们支持哪些时区？

sentences.en: So you mentioned India, the US and the EU, are those, is that pretty much the time zone block or, or what are the requirements?
sentences.zh: 你提到了印度、美国和欧盟，这些就是你们主要覆盖的时区吗，还是说有什么具体要求？

sentences.en: We are flex, we are as flexible as humanly possible in terms of requirements from the individual workers.
sentences.zh: 我们非常灵活，在对个人员工的要求方面，我们尽可能地做到人性化。

sentences.en: So it's very, very flexible for personally.
sentences.zh: 所以对我个人来说，这非常非常灵活。

sentences.en: I'm a night owl.
sentences.zh: 我是个夜猫子。

sentences.en: And that means that I frequently work until 1am in the morning and then logging late in the next, the next, well, the same morning, technically.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我经常工作到凌晨1点，然后很晚才下线，严格来说已经是第二天早上了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 明白。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 那很酷。

sentences.en: Patrick, are you a night owl?
sentences.zh: Patrick，你是夜猫子吗？

sentences.en: Uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 呃，是的。

sentences.en: No morning person.
sentences.zh: 不是早起型的人。

sentences.en: No, I used to be, I used to be, but, uh, with kids, I lost the, the opportunity to do it.
sentences.zh: 不是，我以前是，但有了孩子后，我就没机会早起了。

sentences.en: I still think I would do it if I could.
sentences.zh: 我还是觉得如果可以的话，我还是会选择早起。

sentences.en: If the sun is not shining bright, I'm pretty much getting tired and going to sleep.
sentences.zh: 如果太阳没出来，我基本上就会感到疲倦并去睡觉。

sentences.en: You know, I actually, at a place that Patrick and I used to work a long time ago, I got into a lot of trouble because I just could not show up at, what was it?
sentences.zh: 你知道，其实在Patrick和我很久以前工作过的地方，我惹过很多麻烦，因为我就是没法在那个时间点出现，那是几点来着？

sentences.en: Seven 30 or something.
sentences.zh: 七点半还是什么的。

sentences.en: They were asking us to show up and, uh, I just couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 他们要求我们准时到，但我就是做不到。

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我就说，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: I mean, I had no reason, you know, it's not like I had something at seven 30, but I'm also a night owl.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我没什么理由，你知道，并不是说我七点半有什么事，但我确实是个夜猫子。

sentences.en: I just could not do it.
sentences.zh: 我就是做不到。

sentences.en: And, uh, I would always go in much later than that.
sentences.zh: 而且我总是比那个时间晚到很多。

sentences.en: But, uh, now with kids, I don't have a choice.
sentences.zh: 但现在有了孩子，我没得选了。

sentences.en: They just come in and, and kick, kick the door down, you know, jump on my stomach.
sentences.zh: 他们会直接冲进来，把门踢开，你知道，跳到我肚子上。

sentences.en: And I'm like, okay, I guess we're getting up now, but that's cool.
sentences.zh: 我就想，好吧，看来我们现在得起床了，但这挺好的。

sentences.en: I think that, uh, yeah, I think there's, there is a ton of flexibility there.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，是的，我觉得那里有很大的灵活性。

sentences.en: If you're out there and you are, um, you know, if you're a
sentences.zh: 如果你正在听，如果你是，你知道，如果你是一个

sentences.en: Dask user, if you're a Dask enthusiast, you know, Coiled is, is, uh, hiring folks.
sentences.zh: Dask用户，如果你是Dask的爱好者，你知道，Coiled正在招聘人才。

sentences.en: You know, this is a question we get asked a lot, you know, what's the best way for someone to impress the hiring managers at Coiled?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我们经常被问到的一个问题，就是一个人给Coiled的招聘经理留下深刻印象的最佳方式是什么？

sentences.en: Contribute on both.
sentences.zh: 在两个项目上做贡献。

sentences.en: We have the Dask board on GitHub, Dask Dask, which is the NumPy and Pandas wrapper and the Dask distributed, which is the, uh, scheduling part.
sentences.zh: 我们在GitHub上有Dask板，即Dask Dask，它是NumPy和Pandas的封装，还有Dask distributed，这是调度部分。

sentences.en: We have plenty of tick issue tickets to pick up from, and if you have your own issues and you believe that it may be within your reach, go on and contribute with APR.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多任务单可以认领，如果你有自己的想法，并且认为自己能胜任，那就去提交PR吧。

sentences.en: You will be very, very welcome to do so.
sentences.zh: 我们非常非常欢迎你这样做。

sentences.en: That's how I impressed Matt Rocklin, for example.
sentences.zh: 这就是我给Matt Rocklin留下深刻印象的方式，举个例子。

sentences.en: That's exactly how I was scattered.
sentences.zh: 我当时就是这样被发现的。

sentences.en: I was just contributing.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是在做贡献。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这很有道理。

sentences.en: I submitted a change recently to, uh,
sentences.zh: 我最近提交了一个修改到，呃，

sentences.en: Apache drill.
sentences.zh: Apache drill。

sentences.en: You know, one of the things that just talking to some folks, I realized there's a lot of people don't understand that at the end of the day, all of these things, whether it's Linux
sentences.zh: 你知道，在与一些人交谈时，我意识到很多人不明白，归根结底，所有这些东西，无论是Linux

sentences.en: or, or whether it's Dask or whether it's drill or spark or all of these things at the end of the day are just pieces of software that you can go and look at.
sentences.zh: 还是Dask，或者是Drill、Spark，归根结底都只是你可以去查看的软件。

sentences.en: I mean, if they're open source.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果它们是开源的话。

sentences.en: And so, you know, don't ever, uh, shy away from, you know, going and reading the developer
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，永远不要因为，你知道，去阅读开发者

sentences.en: instructions, you know, building your own local copy of whatever it is and making whatever improvements or fixes you want to make.
sentences.zh: 说明，构建你自己的本地副本，或者进行任何你想要的改进或修复而感到退缩。

sentences.en: You know, I think a lot of people are intimidated by that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为很多人对此感到畏惧。

sentences.en: You know, they say, well, I pip install Dask.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，我用pip安装了Dask。

sentences.en: I don't know how to get the code or how to change the code.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么获取代码，也不知道怎么修改代码。

sentences.en: And it turns out it's not as hard as you would think for any of these projects.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，对于这些项目中的任何一个，这都没有你想象的那么难。

sentences.en: And so I think it's great advice.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个很好的建议。

sentences.en: I just want to double down on that and say, if you think this is interesting, go in and look at how you can have an impact right now.
sentences.zh: 我只想强调这一点，如果你觉得这很有趣，那就去看看你现在能做出什么贡献。

sentences.en: And that's going to be the best way to, uh, you know, signal not only to them, but to yourself, like to tell for you to sort of confirm
sentences.zh: 这将是最好的方式，不仅是向他们，也是向你自己发出信号，让你确认

sentences.en: with yourself that this is something that you really enjoy and are good at.
sentences.zh: 你自己确实喜欢并擅长这件事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's, it's going to be immensely, even if nobody is going to hire you is going to be immensely useful for your career growth and is 100% something that you can put in your CV.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使没有人雇佣你，这对你的职业发展也是非常有用的，而且这绝对可以写进你的简历里。

sentences.en: Frequent Dask contributor.
sentences.zh: Dask的活跃贡献者。

sentences.en: It has a weight on a CV.
sentences.zh: 这在简历上很有分量。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think, uh, you know, just to make this super concrete, we, we had a candidate who had kind of mixed results on the coding part of our interview.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，为了让这一点非常具体，我们曾经有一位候选人在面试的编码环节表现平平。

sentences.en: Um, you know, so we were kind of debating the hiring committee was going back and forth as to what to do about this candidate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们当时在讨论，招聘委员会对于如何处理这位候选人意见不一。

sentences.en: And one of us went to their GitHub and we saw that they had done all this open source work and they had these projects.
sentences.zh: 然后我们其中一人查看了他们的GitHub，发现他们做了所有这些开源工作，并且有这些项目。

sentences.en: They took the time to test it and it was related to our field.
sentences.zh: 他们花时间进行了测试，而且这与我们的领域相关。

sentences.en: And so that actually had a huge impact.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Um, it almost just instantly changed everyone's perspective.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它几乎瞬间改变了每个人的看法。

sentences.en: So, um, you know, so if you do things, you know, and, and, you know, build things that you're proud of and then publish them.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道，如果你做了事情，并且，你知道，构建了你引以为傲的东西，然后发布它们。

sentences.en: So you can be proud of them at least for, for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这样你至少可以为它们感到自豪很长一段时间。

sentences.en: Um, and, and then also kind of broadcast the message to others as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后也把这个信息传播给其他人。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Um, so Guido, if people want to reach out to, you know, either you or other folks at Coiled, um, you know, what's the best way for, uh, folks to kind of follow you
sentences.zh: 嗯，那么Guido，如果人们想联系，你知道，你或其他Coiled的同事，嗯，你知道，大家关注你

sentences.en: and, and know more about what you and what Coiled are up to.
sentences.zh: 并了解你和Coiled在做什么的最佳方式是什么？

sentences.en: So if you are interested in the Dask development, we have the Dask GitHub boards.
sentences.zh: 如果你对Dask开发感兴趣，我们有Dask GitHub板。

sentences.en: We have the community board, which is about the higher level design and direction.
sentences.zh: 我们有社区板，是关于更高层面的设计和方向的。

sentences.en: And then we have the Dask Dask and Dask distributed boards, which are the lower level day-to-day issues.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有Dask Dask和Dask distributed板，是关于底层日常问题的。

sentences.en: We have, uh, I believe our customers lack, we have this course,
sentences.zh: 我们有，呃，我相信我们的客户Slack，我们有这个课程，

sentences.en: we are active on Stack Overflow as well.
sentences.zh: 我们在Stack Overflow上也很活跃。

sentences.en: So if you put a question on Task Overflow about Dask, there is a good chance that some of us may spot it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在Stack Overflow上提关于Dask的问题，我们中的一些人很有可能会看到。

sentences.en: But if you want to make sure, reach out directly.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想确保得到回复，可以直接联系我们。

sentences.en: We have people that are just do that as a job.
sentences.zh: 我们有专门负责做这件事的人。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: When you say Dask, uh, when you say Dask board, I'm actually on the Dask GitHub page now.
sentences.zh: 当你提到Dask，呃，当你提到Dask板时，我其实现在就在Dask GitHub页面上。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你指的是什么？

sentences.en: Uh, the issues page.
sentences.zh: 呃，问题页面（Issues page）。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Oh, got it.
sentences.zh: 哦，明白了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So yeah, check out the issues page and see the, uh, oh yeah, here we go.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，去看看问题页面，看看，呃，哦是的，就是这里。

sentences.en: Monthly community meeting.
sentences.zh: 月度社区会议。

sentences.en: Oh, that is super cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太酷了。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, definitely, if you go to Dask issues, you can actually see, um, you know, the, the issues are also used for, for discussion, which is really neat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以是的，绝对的，如果你去Dask issues，你实际上可以看到，嗯，你知道，这些问题也被用于讨论，这真的很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I've never seen that before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没见过这种情况。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think we can put a book work in this.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以结束这一部分了。

sentences.en: This has been super, super interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常非常有意思。

sentences.en: I think that, oh, uh, before we close out, I wanted to let people know that, you know, this is the, the coiled product.
sentences.zh: 我想，哦，呃，在结束之前，我想让大家知道，你知道，这就是Coiled产品。

sentences.en: Obviously Dask is completely open source for you to use, but also coiled.
sentences.zh: 显然Dask是完全开源供你使用的，但Coiled也是。

sentences.en: Um, if you're a student, if you're getting started, coiled is also free.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你是学生，如果你刚开始学习，Coiled也是免费的。

sentences.en: They have a very generous free tier.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个非常慷慨的免费层级。

sentences.en: You will still pay for your cloud resources.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要支付云资源费用。

sentences.en: Although Amazon also has a bunch of amazing resources for students and you can, you can combine these.
sentences.zh: 尽管亚马逊也为学生提供了大量很棒的资源，你可以把这些结合起来。

sentences.en: They're not exclusive.
sentences.zh: 它们并不冲突。

sentences.en: So, so you can be on the AWS credits that they give students and, uh, use those credits to run coiled completely for free.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以使用他们给学生的AWS额度，并使用这些额度完全免费地运行Coiled。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, even if you, let's say you've already graduated, you could get spun up with coil at a very modest amount.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，即使你，假设你已经毕业了，你也可以用非常适中的费用启动Coiled。

sentences.en: Um, you know, you get to choose what sort of resources that you want to, to, to put forth there and be well within the free tier.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，你可以选择你想要投入的资源类型，并且完全在免费层级之内。

sentences.en: So there's really no reason not to try this out.
sentences.zh: 所以真的没有理由不去尝试一下。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, once you have Dask running locally on your laptop, you could use coiled to run something at a larger scale with a very little, uh, friction.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，一旦你在笔记本电脑上本地运行了Dask，你就可以使用Coiled以极小的阻力在更大规模上运行某些东西。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: And with that, we can, uh, call this a show.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，我们可以，呃，结束节目了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much Guido for coming on.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢Guido的到来。

sentences.en: I mean, we covered a lot of really interesting stuff.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们涵盖了很多非常有趣的内容。

sentences.en: We explained to folks how, um, you know, even if you're writing in C, if you just do four a from zero to 10, uh, uh, that's not going to be as fast as NumPy and why that is.
sentences.zh: 我们向大家解释了，嗯，你知道，即使你用C语言编写，如果你只是做一个从0到10的for循环，呃，那不会像NumPy那样快，以及为什么会这样。

sentences.en: And, and, uh, uh, uh, covered Pandas, covered R, we covered Dask, um, give you a whole bunch of great references.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，涵盖了Pandas，涵盖了R，我们涵盖了Dask，嗯，给你提供了一大堆很棒的参考资料。

sentences.en: Um, we'll put a whole bunch of links here in the show notes to help, help everyone, uh, out there, um, get ramped up on this if you're not already.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们会在节目笔记中放一大堆链接，帮助大家，呃，如果你还没开始，能快速上手。

sentences.en: And, uh, so thanks so much for, for helping to, uh, drive the discussion.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，所以非常感谢你，帮助，呃，推动了这次讨论。

sentences.en: Guido, I really appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: Guido，我真的很感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: No worries.
sentences.zh: 别客气。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.zh: 好了，各位。

sentences.zh: 感谢大家在Patreon和Audible上支持我们。

sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。
